title: Tag and keyword case matching engine

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” audit round 1, commit 0583f53 (branch sprint-4-case-matcher).

Scope audited: lib/concern-fact-pattern-bridge.ts, lib/case-matcher.ts, the
MatchedTag/MatchResult and HumanRightsCodeGround changes in lib/types.ts, and
both new test files. Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict.

All 15 requirements met. All 12 acceptance criteria confirmed. Vitest: 27/27
pass, run twice, identical. tsc --noEmit clean. data/seed-library.json and
package.json untouched. No embeddings/vector/model dependency. Matcher is pure
(no network, fs, clock, randomness), never reads groundTags, never branches on
isPlaceholder. Bridge is a single exported commented constant and is genuinely
many-to-many in both directions (medical-absence -> 3 tags;
disability-accommodation reached from all 4 concerns). types.ts changes are
bounded to requirements 12 and 13.

REQUIRED BEFORE SHIP â€” two fixes, both small:

1. [MEDIUM] The relevance threshold is never exercised at its boundary.
   lib/case-matcher.test.ts:72 "returns empty when nothing clears the relevance
   threshold" uses a situation with an empty narrative, all three facts
   not-reported, and a case whose only fact-pattern tag is outside the bridged
   set. That scores exactly 0. Every other test scores >= 10 (one fact-pattern
   hit = factPatternWeight = 10 = relevanceThreshold). No test produces a score
   strictly between 0 and threshold, so the suite proves only "zero overlap
   returns empty", which is true of any filter, and does not pin the threshold
   at all: any relevanceThreshold from 1 to 10 passes the entire suite
   unchanged. Requirement 8 is the one requirement that exists to stop a weak
   case reaching a user, and it is the one with no test behind it. Add a case
   with keyword overlap only and no bridged fact-pattern overlap â€” 1 to 4
   shared keywords scores 2 to 8, below threshold â€” asserting an empty result.

2. [MEDIUM] Tie-breaking uses String.prototype.localeCompare with no locale
   argument (lib/case-matcher.ts:126). localeCompare resolves against the host's
   default locale and ICU build, so ordering is a property of the machine, not
   of the code. Requirement 6 asks for the same Situation and library to always
   produce the same ordered result. Harmless against the current lowercase-ASCII
   placeholder ids, and it does satisfy the "explicit, not incidental to
   iteration order" half of the requirement, but it is not deterministic by
   construction, and Sprint 7 replaces every id in the library. On a tool whose
   output is which two cases a person is shown, ordering should not depend on
   the build environment. Use a plain codepoint comparison (a < b ? -1 : a > b
   ? 1 : 0) or pass an explicit locale.

MINOR â€” fix while in there, not a gate:

3. [LOW] lib/case-matcher.test.ts:75-76 comment states "age-termination is not
   among medical-absence's bridged patterns". It is â€” medical-absence bridges to
   disability-accommodation, family-status, and age-termination. The test itself
   is correct (the fixture is tagged harassment-poisoned-work-environment); only
   the comment is wrong. It sits in the test documenting threshold behaviour, so
   it is the comment most likely to mislead whoever tunes the bridge later.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER / CHANG â€” not a defect, do not fix in this sprint:

relevanceThreshold (10) equals factPatternWeight (10), so a single bridged
fact-pattern hit clears the gate on its own. Combined with a deliberately broad
bridge, disability-accommodation is reachable from all four concerns, this means
essentially any situation clears the threshold against essentially any case
carrying that tag. The threshold does almost no filtering work in practice.
Requirement 8's mechanism is correctly implemented and weight tuning is
explicitly out of scope (no benchmark set exists), so this is not a failure of
this sprint. It is, however, the specific interaction that decides whether
requirement 8's intent, an empty result beats a bad case, actually holds once
Sprint 7 lands real citations. This belongs with the bridge review already
flagged in the sprint's Dependencies section, and should be settled before
Sprint 6 renders anything.

Placeholder library data was treated as the expected input throughout, per the
sprint's standing instruction. No finding recorded about case content. Noted
only as context: the four placeholder records carry the literal title
[VERIFIED CASE CITATION NEEDED] and near-empty keyFinding text, so the keyword
path contributes nothing against the current library and all matching today is
fact-pattern-only. That is the sprint's stated position (logic provable, quality
not), not a defect, but it does mean the keyword scoring path has no exercise
outside synthetic fixtures until Sprint 7.

Re-audit required after fixes 1 and 2. Do not run /sprint-dev-done on this
verdict.
